newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain's Thatcher to keep close interest in HK.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Thatcher to keep close interest in HK.

text.p: Former British Prime Minister Baroness Thatcher said on Monday she would speak up on Hong Kong issues after the colony reverted to China on July 1.
"I will continue to speak up for Hong Kong's freedom, its rule of law and its elected legislature," Thatcher said after meeting the leader of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, Martin Lee.

"I assured him that my close interest in Hong Kong's affairs will continue beyond the handover of sovereignty in June," said Thatcher, who negotiated the 1984 Joint Declaration, the treaty between Beijing and London covering the sovereignty change.
The treaty allows Hong Kong to run its own affairs and keep its capitalist way of life for 50 years after the handover.

But Beijing has recently launched plans to curb civil and political rights and roll back democracy in the territory. It has also appointed a provisional legislature to replace the present elected body, thereby sidelining Lee's Democrats.

Lee said he was happy to meet Thatcher and find she continued to be firm against changes to be made to Hong Kong by China. "Based on our meeting, I believe Lady Thatcher is very concerned to see that basic freedoms are not rolled back.
"She believes that the solemn international promises made to Hong Kong people in 1984 must be honoured, and honoured in full," Lee said in a statement.
Thatcher has been in Hong Kong since Friday. On Sunday she inaugurated the world's longest rail and road suspension bridge, providing transport links to Hong Kong's future airport.
